name: The Remnant and the People of God

objectives.text: Retell how God saved Noah and his family in the ark when the flood came on the earth
Identify God's promise to Abraham to make his family into a great people through whom all nations would be blessed
Describe how Joshua and Caleb trusted God when most of Israel refused to enter the land
Summarize the account of Elijah in which God tells him of 7,000 in Israel who had not bowed to Baal
Describe John's vision of a great multitude from every nation worshiping God as the whole people of God gathered together
Explain the biblical meaning of remnant as the part of God's people whom He preserves through judgment
Describe how God preserved a remnant of Judah through the exile and brought them back to rebuild Jerusalem
Compare the crowds who left Jesus with the disciples who stayed when His teaching became hard
Identify biblical names and images for the people of God such as flock, vine, holy nation, and bride
Explain the Reformed teaching that Christ gathers, defends, and preserves His church as the people called out by Him
Explain how the covenant promise I will be their God and they will be my people runs through the whole Bible
Analyze how the prophets join warnings of judgment on unfaithful Israel with promises of a preserved remnant
Analyze how Paul uses the example of Elijah to show that the remnant exists by God's election of grace
Interpret Paul's olive tree metaphor to explain how Gentile believers are grafted into the one people of God
Explain how the New Testament presents Jesus as the faithful Israel in whom the people of God are gathered
Distinguish the invisible church from the visible church as the Westminster Confession defines them
Explain the Reformed teaching that the visible church consists of those who profess the true religion together with their children
Explain the marks of the true church as the Reformed confessions state them and their basis in Scripture
Construct a timeline of the remnant theme from Genesis to Revelation that cites key passages and explains each stage
Evaluate episodes from church history in light of the confessional teaching that Christ will always preserve a church on earth despite error and decline
Defend from Scripture the faithfulness of God to His covenant promises in times of widespread apostasy
Compare the Reformed covenantal view of the continuity of Israel and the church with the dispensational view using key texts
Analyze the main interpretations of Paul's statement that all Israel will be saved within the argument of Romans 9 to 11

changes: Replaced vague early items (God always has friends, not everyone listens, God keeps His people safe) with concrete, assessable story objectives on Noah, Abraham, Joshua and Caleb, and Elijah. Kept and reworded the remnant definition, crowds vs disciples, olive tree, election, visible/invisible church, remnant history, preservation of the church, God's faithfulness, and Israel/church continuity, anchoring each to specific verses and accurate confessional articles (added WCF 25.2, 25.5, 7.5-7.6, Heidelberg Q54, Belgic 29). Moved the Galatians 6:16 reference to the continuity objective. Added missing competencies: exile and return, Revelation 7 multitude, biblical images for God's people, the covenant formula, prophetic judgment and remnant, Christ as true Israel, covenant children in the visible church, marks of the church, and interpretations of Romans 11:26. Dropped the vague faithful minority item, now covered by the prophetic and Pauline analysis objectives.
